messages.subject: compiling rapache for Mac Leopard 64-bit
messages.body_plain:
A prior post noted that the configure script fails for 64-bit MacOS.
I am running Leopard 10.5.8. I just got it working, so I thought I
would pass along some tips.  WARNING I am not at all comfortable with
configure, make, etc. so I am sure to leave out some things; buyer
beware.

I will assume you have made the changes in httpd.conf as described in
the manual.

As indicated in the prior post, the problem is solved by compiling
both libapreq2 and rapache for the 64-bit architecture.

STEP 0: you have a problem

$ apachectl configtest
gives you an error about mod_R.so, for example, the architecture is
incorrect (meaning it was compiled for 32-bit but Apache is 64-bit)

STEP 1: Compile libapreq2  for x86_64.

$ cd rapache-1.1.9/libapreq2/library
$ ./configure

edit the Makefile to change:
CFLAGS =  -g -O2
to
CFLAGS =  -g -O2 -arch x86_64

I am not sure if you need to also change:
LDFLAGS =
to
LDFLAGS = -arch x86_64

note - at this point, if there are any xxxx.o or xxxx.lo files, for
example from a prior compilation attempt, they should be deleted.  If
there are any files in the ./.libs/ directory they should be deleted
too.

$make

this should run with no errors (a few nonfatal warnings are OK), and
leave only 64-bit files:

$ file .libs/*
.libs/cookie.o:              Mach-O 64-bit object x86_64
.libs/error.o:               Mach-O 64-bit object x86_64
.libs/libapreq2.3.1.0.dylib: Mach-O 64-bit dynamically linked shared
library x86_64
.libs/module.o:              Mach-O 64-bit object x86_64
.libs/module_cgi.o:          Mach-O 64-bit object x86_64
.libs/module_custom.o:       Mach-O 64-bit object x86_64
.libs/param.o:               Mach-O 64-bit object x86_64
.libs/parser.o:              Mach-O 64-bit object x86_64
.libs/parser_header.o:       Mach-O 64-bit object x86_64
.libs/parser_multipart.o:    Mach-O 64-bit object x86_64
.libs/parser_urlencoded.o:   Mach-O 64-bit object x86_64
.libs/util.o:                Mach-O 64-bit object x86_64
.libs/version.o:             Mach-O 64-bit object x86_64

However, I think I left out one key step that is required to get
libapreq2.3.1.0.dylib into 64-bit...this needs to be solved.
Unfortunately I can't remember what I did; I may have used an editor
to cut & paste the command generated by make:

gcc -dynamiclib -flat_namespace -undefined suppress -o .libs/
libapreq2.3.1.0.dylib  .libs/util.o .libs/version.o .libs/
cookie.o .libs/param.o .libs/parser.o .libs/parser_urlencoded.o .libs/
parser_header.o .libs/parser_multipart.o .libs/module.o .libs/
module_custom.o .libs/module_cgi.o .libs/error.o  -L/usr/lib -lapr-1 -
laprutil-1 -lsqlite3 /usr/lib/libexpat.dylib /usr/lib/libiconv.dylib -
lpthread -install_name  /usr/lib/libapreq2.3.dylib -
compatibility_version 5 -current_version 5.0

to add the -arch x86_64 option, then delete all the libapreq2 files,
and run the new command. Ugly, but it worked.

$ sudo make install

STEP 2: Compile/install rapache

The following options for configure solve most of the problems.  I am
trying to get apxs to take the options -Wc,-arch -Wc,x86_64 -Wl,-arch -
Wl,x86_64.  The backslashes are to prevent them from being passed as
options to configure.  There must be a better way since I still get an
error message, but the Makefile seems correct.

./configure --with-apache2-apxs=/usr/sbin/apxs\ -Wc,-arch\ -Wc,x86_64\
-Wl,-arch\ -Wl,x86_64 CFLAGS=-arch\ x86_64

I don't know how to prevent the error in:
RINCLUDES = -I/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/include -I/
Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/include/i386

Which I changed in the Makefile by replacing "i386" with "x86_64"

$ make

Success can be verified with this command:
$ file .libs/*
.libs/mod_R.a:   current ar archive random library
.libs/mod_R.la:  ASCII English text
.libs/mod_R.lai: ASCII English text
.libs/mod_R.o:   Mach-O 64-bit object x86_64
.libs/mod_R.so:  Mach-O 64-bit bundle x86_64

If any of these say i386 instead of x86_64 then an option was not set
somewhere along the way.

$ sudo make install

That's the best I can do for now.

-b

--

messages.subject: How to insert R value into a form
messages.subject_clean: How to insert R value into a form
messages.body_plain:
At the beginning of my code I define startDate

startDate <- ifelse(is.null(GET$startDate),Sys.Date(),GET$startDate)

and it works fine, but I want to use startDate as the default value in
my form.

Date (mm/dd/yyyy)<INPUT TYPE="text" NAME="startDate" SIZE=25
value=startDate>

The above doesn't work because it shows "startDate" instead of the
value of startDate.  Can anyone tell me the how to do this?

TIA, Roger

--

messages.subject: Re: RApache and .Rdata
messages.body_plain:
It's possible, but I don't know where the files should reside.  A
basic issue is that of read/write permissions; RApache must have
proper permissions to read and write the RData file wherever it is.

-bb

--
